Teton Digital CUP Application Denial Appeal — Staff Memorandum

patch.longFormSummary:
• The presentation budgets $45M Phase I and $155M Phase II and describes a company-built 100 MW substation. The old $450M and Aurum ownership are unsupported. It proposes a 25-acre subdivision from an approximately 80-acre parent site.
  • The staff memo identifies S½ NW¼ Section 4, T155N R95W, parcel 12-155-95-00-04-039. The corrected context point approximates that legal description using BLM section geometry; it is not a surveyed subdivision boundary.
  • The February 18 action allowed the data-center appeal; it was not a battery approval or proof of final CUP, construction or operation.
  • Timeline: October 1, 2026 is a Q3/Q4-2026 phase-two target placeholder from the February 2025 presentation. The target is unverified; Phase I’s Q3/Q4-2025 target is past, not proof of service.
  • Trinity 1 applicant’s site-context diagram showing proposed 25-acre subdivision and MWEC substation; historical February 2025 proposal, not verified construction. Credit: Teton Digital / Williams County February 2025 filing; underlying aerial map as credited in source.

patch.title: Hecate Otter Creek Solar: 1 GW / $1B Coffey County Proposal
patch.description: Hecate’s actual Coffey County proposal is Otter Creek Solar: 1 GW, potentially in two phases, about 8,500 leased acres west of Burlington and a published approximately $1B private investment plan. It is proposed, not confirmed under construction.

researchNotes: Content maintenance under standing authorization. No application changes, build, restart or production deployment.
PJM MFO is total facility output, MWE is the incremental energy request in these studies and MWC is capacity rights; none is battery MWh. Used explicit storage specifications and related requests.

Historical regulatory/study/public-information events replace unsupported CODs for Oystercatcher, Oak Run, Jay, Prologis, Clover–Rawlings, Heritage–Wake, Jupiter, Sabey and Otter Creek. These dates are not opening dates.
MISO J4194 has applicationStatus Active and withdrawnDate 2026-06-11; do not silently classify it as either operating or cancelled. The queue provides no developer identity.

SPP GEN-2025-SR1 is surplus storage sharing an existing solar 400 MW export limit. Study equipment is 475 MW DC / 418 MW AC, distinct from requested 400 MW service. Clinton is a queue location, not proof of Clinton County.
CAISO HOODINI 1663: 450 MW storage, 459.54 MW PV, 450 MW net export, SDGE, December 31, 2031. Power row represents the solar component; do not sum hybrid capacities into export.

Location markers are sourced/qualified context points. Trinity uses BLM Section 4 T155N R95W geometry and S-half NW-quarter approximation; this is not a surveyed 25-acre subdivision. Other new points use operator/county maps, a regulator POI or address/city geocodes, not final site boundaries.

Official galleries and linked project documents checked. PointOne render is labelled conceptual. Prologis and Teton diagrams are embedded originals from opened primary PDFs. NAS Lemoore/Chirisa downloads were blocked or returned thin shells; no unrelated stock photo substituted. Butte committee images were decorative and Otter Creek boards include an unrelated Upshur Texas solar photo, neither used as site photography.

PJM Phase II studies, SPP active listing and report, fresh MISO API, valid same-day CAISO/EIA workbooks and ISO-NE QP1143 approval letter inspected. Later direct CAISO download hit certificate validation; EIA XLSX URL returned HTML, so neither was counted as a fresh workbook. BLM old PDF URL returned registry HTML, leaving the exact Monte Cristo Phase 1 identity unresolved.

No globally refreshed translations, source wikis, stock associations, unchanged outlines or retained approximate coordinates. API auto-linked the exact Prologis/Sabey company names to their matching company wiki URLs; those links were retained.
No credit balance is available; this checkpoint does not claim a measured low-credit threshold.
